facts.statement: The study investigated how cognitive test score variability differed among three racial and ethnic groups and whether primary language predicted this variability in Mexican Americans.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study included 4,140 older adults from the HABS-HD study, with an average age of 65.08 years, who completed cognitive tests in either English or Spanish.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Cognitive status was associated with test score variability, with cognitively normal participants showing lower variability than those with mild cognitive impairment or dementia, a pattern that held across all three groups.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Primary language was associated with test score variability, and Spanish-speaking Mexican Americans showed higher variability than Non-Hispanic Whites, Non-Hispanic Blacks, and English-speaking Mexican Americans.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The association between primary language and test score variability remained significant even after adjusting for additional factors and became stronger when using residualized measures.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: When comparing only English-speaking Mexican Americans to Non-Hispanic Whites, the former group still showed higher test score variability, and this difference increased when using residualized measures.
facts.subject: humans
